description: Section 5 (backend, built-but-gated-off): implement the BLOG_CONTRIBUTION payment purpose end to end - a server that authoritatively decides the contribution amount in integer paise, creates a Razorpay gateway order behind the SAME disabled initiation/readiness gate, verifies the result by authoritative provider readback + webhook with idempotency and reconciliation, and stores only the required authoritative records. A contribution does NOT create a Wix Store product/order. No real charge is enabled.
steps: Study the existing patterns before writing: amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/website_checkout.py (gated prepare_checkout + verify_callback), checkout_pricing.py + money.py (integer paise), order_keys.py (reference mint/reserve, gateway-order binding, request-key reservation, one-time conditional claims, capture quarantine), payment_attempt.py (attempt state machine), integrations/razorpay_orders.py (create_order, account_mode), integrations/razorpay_verify.py (authoritative captured-payment readback), and payments/razorpay-webhook/handler.py especially the partner_billing.topup branch where payment.notes are NEVER authority and an idempotency claim keyed by payment id is conditional.

Add a BLOG_CONTRIBUTION purpose constant and the server-side amount authority: a module (e.g. amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/blog_contribution.py) that validates a requested amount against an authoritative allowed set/range (mirroring src/config/contribution.ts presets + custom bounds, defined server-side so the browser cannot widen it), in integer paise, rejecting fractional paise / out-of-range / non-INR. The server amount is authoritative; the browser value is only a request.

Implement contribution initiation reusing the website_checkout gating shape: a prepare-contribution function that (1) validates postId/slug and the server-authoritative amount, (2) reserves a reference/attempt via order_keys + payment_attempt with checkoutMode/purpose = BLOG_CONTRIBUTION, (3) is gated by the SAME CHECKOUT_INITIATION_ENABLED env (default off) and the readiness inputs (EXPECTED_CONFIGURATION_NAME/MID empty => not ready): gate off returns PAYMENT_INITIATION_DISABLED with no gateway order and no payable attempt; gate on returns only the browser-safe options (public keyId, stored gateway orderId, amountPaise, currency, prefill, paymentAttemptId). NO constant may force it on.

Implement contribution verification reusing website_checkout.verify_callback shape + razorpay_verify: HMAC over the SERVER-STORED gateway order id (never the browser's), re-check stored account/mode (test must not settle live), require an authoritative captured-payment readback whose amount/currency equal the stored binding before a VERIFIED/CAPTURED state. A valid signature alone is only a trigger, never proof.

Implement the webhook path for BLOG_CONTRIBUTION in/alongside payments/razorpay-webhook/handler.py mirroring the topup pattern: HMAC-verified event, idempotency log, a conditional one-time claim keyed by payment id, amount re-derived from the stored attempt/binding (NOT from payment.notes), single-settlement, and quarantine for paid-but-unresolvable captures (reconcilable via the existing reconcile scripts pattern). A BLOG_CONTRIBUTION capture must NOT create a Wix Store product/order.

Define and store ONLY the required authoritative records (new DynamoDB record shape or extension of the existing commerce-keys/attempt tables, matching repo conventions): contribution ID, blog post ID, slug, amount in paise, currency, payment attempt ID, Razorpay order ID, Razorpay payment ID, verified/captured state, timestamps, and refund state where applicable. No PII beyond opaque ids; follow the no-plaintext-logging rule (event names/opaque ids/states/counts only).

Write real pytest coverage in tests/ driving the ACTUAL contribution handler/functions against tests/crm_fake_dynamo.py with a stubbed Razorpay readback (not static mocks). Cover: gate-off returns PAYMENT_INITIATION_DISABLED and creates no gateway order/payable attempt; amount validation (preset accepted, out-of-range/fractional/non-INR rejected); signature-only is not proof (NOT_CAPTURED without readback); binding/amount/currency mismatch rejected; test-mode cannot settle live; webhook idempotency (replay of same payment id settles once); notes are not authority (forged notes amount ignored); quarantine of paid-but-blocked; no Wix product/order side effect. Add revert-checks: a test that FAILS if the gate/readiness guard or the notes-not-authority guard is reverted.

Deliver the AWS-dependent wiring (new route/function registration, IAM, env, Razorpay account binding) as source + a precise runbook under docs/execution/ following the prior website-checkout runbook precedent, and mark it BLOCKED-ON-ENVIRONMENT: no AWS credentials in sandbox, so no deploy/live-verify. Keep CHECKOUT_INITIATION_ENABLED off and readiness unset. Do NOT execute or fake any live call. Any chat-pasted AWS key MUST NOT be used.
Commit to feature/customer-experience-upgrade with explicit-path staging only.
acceptance_criteria: A BLOG_CONTRIBUTION purpose exists with a server-authoritative integer-paise amount validator; the browser cannot set or widen the trusted amount.

Initiation is gated by the SAME CHECKOUT_INITIATION_ENABLED gate (default off) and readiness: gate off => PAYMENT_INITIATION_DISABLED, no gateway order, no payable attempt; no constant can force it on.

Verification requires HMAC over the stored order id PLUS an authoritative captured-payment readback matching the stored binding; a bare signature/query string/browser callback/frontend state is never accepted as proof.

The webhook settles exactly once per payment id (idempotent), re-derives amount from stored records not from payment.notes, quarantines paid-but-unresolvable captures, and creates NO Wix Store product/order.
Only the required authoritative records are stored; no plaintext PII is logged.
Real pytest tests drive the actual handlers against the in-memory DynamoDB fake with stubbed readback and include revert-checks that fail if a security guard is reverted; full pytest suite passes.
AWS-dependent deploy/live-verify is delivered as source + runbook and reported BLOCKED-ON-ENVIRONMENT, not executed or faked; the gate stays disabled.
verification: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q (new BLOG_CONTRIBUTION tests + full suite pass; record counts)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q -k contribution (focused run shows the new tests exercise the real handler, including revert-checks)
npx tsc --noEmit (if any shared TS types touched)
findings: DONE on branch feature/customer-experience-upgrade. ENDPOINT/ROUTE + ACTIONS: the shipped UI (src/components/BlogContribution.tsx) POSTs {purpose:'BLOG_CONTRIBUTION', postId, slug, amountPaise, currency} to `${NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE||'https://wecare.digital/api'}/ecommerce/contribution`. Backend logic is handler-free business functions in amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/ecommerce/blog_contribution.py: prepare_contribution (initiation) and verify_contribution_callback (browser-result verify), modelled directly on website_checkout.prepare_checkout/verify_callback; plus settle_contribution_capture (webhook). The response status strings are the SAME website-checkout contract the UI branches on (PAYMENT_INITIATION_DISABLED, CHECKOUT_OPTIONS_READY, CHECKOUT_REJECTED, CHECKOUT_AMBIGUOUS), returned verbatim, so the shipped UI binds with NO change. NO DEVIATION from the shipped contract. The HTTP handler wiring the /ecommerce/contribution route to prepare_contribution (plus a verify action) is delivered as the runbook (deferred to deploy time exactly as the website-checkout prepare_checkout/verify_callback handlers are - neither has an HTTP handler committed yet; they ship ahead of the owner architecture decision inside the same wecare-checkout function). AUTH POSTURE: a contribution may be made signed-in OR anonymously (customer_id optional); when absent the request key is scoped under an 'anon' owner marker. This NEVER weakens payment authority because the SERVER decides the amount (validate_contribution_amount) and the webhook re-derives the amount from the stored record - an anonymous caller cannot set or widen the trusted amount, create a second payable order (request-key coordination), or settle anything (capture readback + idempotency claim). A handler wiring the route should follow checkout/handler.py's gate-AND-readiness evaluation; auth is advisory for contributions, not load-bearing for money-safety. FEE DECISION: a voluntary contribution is NOT a commerce collection, so it is NOT run through the FEAT-001 convenience-fee + GST calculator (checkout_pricing.py). The reader is charged EXACTLY the chosen amount in integer paise, nothing added on top (test_enabled_creates_bound_order_with_browser_safe_options_only asserts created['amount_paise']==9900 for a ₹99 choice). Documented in the module docstring; if accounting later wants a fee that is a deliberate change there, not a silent default. RECORD SHAPE/TABLE: new BLOGCONTRIB#<id> row in the existing commerce-keys table (stack-wecare-digital-WixOrderIds, same table as GATEWAYORDER#/REQUESTKEY#/CAPTUREQUARANTINE#), via order_keys.reserve_contribution/resolve_contribution/bind_contribution_gateway_order/mark_contribution_settled. Stores ONLY the required authoritative fields: contributionId, postId, slug, amountPaise, currency, paymentAttemptId, gatewayOrderId, providerPaymentId, state (INITIATED->CAPTURED), refundState (NONE), settledAmountPaise, createdAt/updatedAt/settledAt. No PII; opaque ids only; logging is event-names/ids/states only. GATE/READINESS: prepare_contribution takes an injected initiation_enabled boolean (the handler ANDs CHECKOUT_INITIATION_ENABLED env, default OFF, with payment readiness; EXPECTED_CONFIGURATION_NAME/EXPECTED_PROVIDER_MID empty => not ready). No module constant can force it on - the ONLY path that creates a gateway order is guarded by that boolean. Gate off returns PAYMENT_INITIATION_DISABLED with NO gateway order and NO payable attempt (the contribution record is reserved pre-create but stays INITIATED). The amount validator runs BEFORE the gate, so a disabled gate never launders a widened amount. WEBHOOK: settle_contribution_capture mirrors _handle_wallet_topup_captured. The real razorpay-webhook handler._handle_payment_captured branches on notes.purpose=='BLOG_CONTRIBUTION' to _handle_blog_contribution_captured and returns (does NOT fall through to the invoice/order path). Settlement: (1) requires a STORED contribution record for the notes' contributionId (no record => quarantine); (2) RE-DERIVES amount from the stored record, NEVER from payment.notes, and verifies the capture against Razorpay's API (payment_is_captured), requiring provider amount==record amount in INR to the paise (mismatch/wrong-currency/not-captured => quarantine via record_capture_quarantine, keyed by payment id); (3) conditional one-time settlement claim keyed by payment id (claim_contribution_settlement) BEFORE any state write, so a replay settles exactly once (SETTLE_DUPLICATE). CONFIRM NO WIX ORDER: a BLOG_CONTRIBUTION capture advances only the contribution record - it creates NO Wix Store product, NO purchase order, mints NO public order number (test_webhook_settlement_creates_no_order_identity asserts no PAYMENTATTEMPT#/ORDERNO# rows and resolve_order_for_payment is None). REVERT-CHECK TEST NAMES: tests/test_blog_contribution.py::test_disabled_gate_creates_no_gateway_order (fails if the initiation gate is reverted - create_order is a pytest.fail stub) and ::test_webhook_notes_amount_is_not_authority (fails if the notes-not-authority guard is reverted - forged notes amount 990000 ignored, 4900 re-derived from the stored record and settled). RUNBOOK (BLOCKED-ON-ENVIRONMENT): docs/execution/blog-contribution-provisioning-runbook-2026-10-01.md, modelled on the website-checkout runbook: adds the POST /ecommerce/contribution route on the existing wecare-checkout function (no new function/IAM/env - reuses the same table, Razorpay secret and DISABLED gate), notes the webhook already routes the purpose, and an authorized cancel-only live monetary test. No AWS creds in sandbox, so nothing executed or faked. PACKAGE COMPLETENESS: added lambda_utils/ecommerce/blog_contribution.py to the REQUIRED list in tests/test_checkout_package_completeness.py so it ships in the wecare-checkout deploy ZIP once the route is wired (sibling of website_checkout.py). PYTEST COUNTS (true, post-change): full suite 6042 passed / 1 skipped (baseline 6001/1, +41 new); focused `-k contribution` 41 passed / 5965 deselected; the real razorpay-webhook handler is exercised by test_real_webhook_handler_routes_blog_contribution_and_settles. tsc NOT run: no shared TS types touched (the frontend contract shipped in FEAT-003). Note: order_keys.py already carried the BLOGCONTRIB# primitives and the webhook routing + blog_contribution.py were present uncommitted from an earlier pass; this run verified them end to end, authored the missing runbook, added the package-completeness entry, and committed the whole feature.
